SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number ? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat transfer? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat transfer.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat transfer.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Heat transfer.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat transfer.

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Pollution? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Pollution.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Pollution.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water Pollution.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Pollution.

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Human Breathing System? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Human Breathing System.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Human Breathing System.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Human Breathing System.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Human Breathing System.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution ? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Classification of Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Classification of Plants.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Classification of Plants.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Classification of Plants.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Classification of Plants.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

15. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number of lessons 120 NOTE: The sugg? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number of lessons 120 NOTE: The sugg.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number of lessons 120 NOTE: The sugg.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number of lessons 120 NOTE: The sugg.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number of lessons 120 NOTE: The sugg.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Sound Energy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Heat transfer and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
